objective.text: Select a test that detects rewriting text newly produced by an earlier replacement rule.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish one-pass token substitution from sequential application of replacement pairs.

runtime.sapi: CLI unless the stated context specifies otherwise
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; no custom handler unless explicitly shown. 64-bit PHP; UTC; C locale.

assumptions: Run in a fresh PHP process using only the displayed files and inputs.

The one-character tokens a and b must map to b and c respectively in one pass over the original text. Newly generated b characters must not be processed again. Other characters remain unchanged. All input is ASCII.

files.source:
<?php

function translateTokens(string $text): string
{
    $map = ['a' => 'b', 'b' => 'c'];

    return str_replace(array_keys($map), array_values($map), $text);
}

records.stem: Which input/output case exposes the implementation’s cascading replacement?

options.rationale: Only the second replacement acts, so sequential and one-pass semantics agree.
options.misconception: Testing a rule whose output is not another rule’s input.

options.rationale: The first replacement makes b and the second rewrites it to c, violating the required one-pass result.
Neither replacement changes c, so this does not exercise generated text.
options.misconception: Using an unchanged character to test replacement ordering.

options.text: An empty string → an empty string
options.rationale: Both implementations preserve empty input; no rule runs.
options.misconception: Treating an empty edge case as coverage of a nonempty interaction.

explanation.summary: str_replace applies array search/replacement pairs in sequence, so later pairs can rewrite earlier output. strtr with a mapping does not search the newly inserted replacement text again.
explanation.trace: For a, the defective helper performs a → b → c. The required operation performs only the original a → b substitution.

objective.text: Test that literal regex construction escapes the chosen pattern delimiter as well as regex metacharacters.

difficulty.rationale: Select a fixture that separates regex-body quoting from protection of its surrounding PHP pattern delimiter.

runtime.sapi: CLI unless the stated context specifies otherwise
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; no custom handler unless explicitly shown. 64-bit PHP; UTC; C locale.

assumptions: Run in a fresh PHP process using only the displayed files and inputs.

Every needle must be interpreted literally inside a ~ delimited pattern. The handler captures pattern-construction warnings so the fixture can inspect preg_match’s false result; it does not turn an invalid pattern into a valid non-match. Inputs are ASCII.

files.source:
<?php

set_error_handler(static function (int $severity, string $message): bool {
    return true;
});

function literalMatch(string $needle, string $text): int|false
{
    $pattern = '~' . preg_quote($needle) . '~';

    return preg_match($pattern, $text);
}

records.stem: Which needle/text pair should match but exposes the missing delimiter argument to preg_quote?

options.rationale: preg_quote already escapes the dot metacharacter without needing the delimiter argument.
options.misconception: Testing regex syntax escaping without testing the surrounding delimiter.

options.rationale: The slash is not this pattern’s delimiter, and it needs no delimiter escaping here.
options.misconception: Assuming the conventional slash delimiter is used despite the displayed ~.

options.rationale: The unescaped ~ terminates the pattern prematurely, producing a pattern error instead of the required match.
The brackets are ordinary regex metacharacters that preg_quote already handles.
options.misconception: Choosing another metacharacter covered by the existing default quoting.

explanation.summary: preg_quote can escape both regex-special characters and an explicitly supplied delimiter. Because this helper surrounds the result with ~, it must pass ~ as that second argument.
explanation.trace: The defective tilde needle constructs ~~~, which is not the intended literal-tilde pattern. Quoting with the ~ delimiter produces a valid pattern matching the original tilde character.
